card.name: Final piece of a drug name before dose
card.fires_on: The last piece of a generic drug name (apixaban, infliximab, troleandomycin, cabozantinib) right before the word dose or product. It also fires on hedging adverbs like particularly or usually before a qualifier.

modes.label: Drug name ending
modes.description: Closing piece of a generic drug name in a phrase such as 'depend on the ___ dose'.
modes.example: dosing recommendations for co-administration of apixaban with PREZCOBIX or PREZCOBIX PED depend on the apix<<aban>> dose.

modes.label: Hedging adverb
modes.description: Adverbs like particularly or usually that open a parenthetical qualifier.
modes.example: gastrointestinal toxicity has been reported with concomitant administration of methotrexate (<<usually>> in high dosage)

card.writes: It seems to hold back words like popular or ranked, which suggests it pushes toward a plain next word such as dose or product.
card.plain: It lights up at the end of a drug's name when the text goes on to say 'dose' or 'product', and at words like 'usually' that open a qualifier.
